prompt: Use Bambi to demonstrate hierarchical logistic regression of survey support with a small reproducible synthetic dataset, clearly labeled as synthetic. Include support (0=no, 1=yes), age, income_bracket (low/medium/high), urban (0/1), and region; make some regions smaller than others. Use low income as the reference and a varying intercept by region. Check resolved priors and prior predictions, fit the model, and report the posterior-mean probability of support at age 40, medium income, urban=1 in a specified observed region, with a 94% HDI. Save a diagnostic report and artifacts, reporting failed or unavailable checks and the limits of a small synthetic example. Use the available Bambi 0.21/PyMC 6 environment.
assertions: Uses Bambi with an explicit Bernoulli likelihood, a logit link, and a varying intercept for region
Verifies the modeled support event and the actual low-income reference coding, rather than assuming C(), categorical=, or an unordered category list establishes the baseline
Records predictor transformations and unequal group sizes, preserving training encoding when creating prediction data
Inspects resolved Bambi priors, evaluates prior predictions on probability or replicated support-rate scales, and justifies overrides before fitting
Uses supported Bambi fit and prediction APIs and saves the sampling output before downstream processing
Reports the posterior-mean support probability for age 40, medium income and urban=1 in a named observed region, with an explicit 94% HDI and no confusion with an average or unseen-region target
Uses Bambi's log-density bridge and keeps original-data observed/predictive groups and coordinates compatible with the shared Bayesian diagnostic helpers
Reports convergence, calibration and sensitivity evidence honestly, including missing or failed checks and the limitations of synthetic or smoke-sized inference
Writes the canonical results-folder report.md using shared check_report.json assessments and includes the formula, family/link, event/reference coding and prediction target
